title: “Out of Order” is produced by Most Unwanted Productions at the East V...
transcript: here in the hyper intimate East Village basement this artist draws index cards randomly from a bowl each one prompting one of many short segments of the show which range from wacky monologues from the perspective of farm animals to looking through the performers actual bank statements projected onto the wall and sprinkled throughout there's also a lot of audience participate this is out of order a show created by Carl Holder which had elements that reminded me of shows like Burnout Paradise or the Neo Futurists if you're paying very close attention to my content you might be thinking hang on didn't you make that exact same comparison in your video about ha ha ha ha ha ha ha yes I did you know why it's not a coincidence it's because as I am actively seeking out shows like this this is like the sensibility the approach to theatre that I find most exciting these days and I am going out of my way to find them and post about them for you because like I've said before this feels like live theatre at its most live and out of order is another one that is wildly entertaining but also has an emotional undercurrent even though the disparate pieces of the show are mostly very fun together they form a collage of his struggles with finding happiness and confidence and fulfilment in a career that didn't turn out the way he wanted it to and now you might be thinking is this show kind of a pity party for a struggling artist? and it's a fair question because I have seen shows that explored similar feelings that are actually just kind of sad and uncomfortable to watch honestly I think this show gets very close to falling in that trap but ultimately doesn't because they lean into it in a way that feels deliberate and self aware so it doesn't feel like “woe is me!” as much as we're actually digging into something deep about disrupting pessimistic spirals through art and community
